paragraphs: Rav Pinchas son of Rav Chisda.

[Kiddushin 32b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.32b.2) relates that he and his brother Rav Mari were at the wedding feast of Rava’s son (and if their father was the Rav Chisda generally meant by that name, Rava was their brother-in-law). Rava raised a cup to Rav Pappa and to Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua, and they rose before him. He raised it to Rav Mari and Rav Pinchas, ‘son’—which should read ‘sons’—of Rav Chisda, but they did not rise before him, and he took offense.[^1]

In Ketubot 61a, Rav Pinchas and Rav Mari, sons of Rav Chisda: one would serve food early (to the attendant), while the other served it late. Elijah would converse with the one who served early, etc. In Bava Kamma 117a, we find Rav Mari (spelled מארי), son of Rav Pinchas, son of R. H.; the reading cited as דק״ס is ‘Rav Mari and R. P., sons of R. Ch.’[^2]

notes.text: Hyman prints Kiddushin לב., meaning 32a. The English citation is corrected to the matching account in the checked William Davidson edition, Kiddushin 32b, paragraph 2; the printed 32a is retained here to make the correction explicit. That passage supports expanding ר״פ and ר״ה בריה דר״י as Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua. The conditional brother-in-law identification and the correction from ‘son’ to ‘sons’ are Hyman’s own comments.

Rav Chisda in the Ketubot account follows the immediate heading and family context. In the final textual variant, the initials R. H. (ר״ה), R. P. (ר״פ), and R. Ch. (ר״ח), and the source label דק״ס, are retained without asserting a new genealogy or identifying its edition. The two spellings מרי and מארי are preserved in this note. Ketubot 61a and Bava Kamma 117a are Hyman’s citations and were not independently checked.
